$comment: AI-readiness assessment matrix derived from the assessment matrix of González-Espinoza et al. (2026) — Table 13 (tab:assessment-matrix) in the current draft. Pointers into the paper are given as LaTeX labels with the number of the current draft, because float numbers move whenever a section is inserted; the label does not. 7 Bridge2AI dimensions × 3 readiness levels (L1/L2/L3 ↔ DRL bands C/B/A). Cumulative semantics: Pathway A requires every L1 criterion; Pathway B requires every L1 + L2; Pathway C requires every L1 + L2 + L3. Each matrix cell expands to one to five independently checkable criteria, so the criterion count is larger than the 21 cells. The Croissant descriptor lives at L2 but is marked recommended at L1 to keep upgrades frictionless. Pathway C sub-domain overlays live in pathways.json, not here — they may target any dimension, and a sub-domain may also reword a criterion below via 'label_overrides' (wording only; id, evidence_type, and pathway membership are never changed). All six schema files move in lockstep from 0.9.0; 1.0.0 is cut when the criterion ids are considered stable.
$cells_comment: The 21 cells of the paper's assessment matrix (Table 13, tab:assessment-matrix), quoted verbatim. Held here rather than in a UI constant so the cell wording and the criteria that operationalise it cannot drift apart; the start page and any crosswalk render from this. Each cell expands to one to five criteria below. A criterion whose requirement the cell text does not name carries a 'beyond_cell' object saying where in the paper it does come from — matrix.test.js asserts every cell is populated, every criterion lands in a declared cell, and every extension is attributed.

FAIRness.L2: FAIR I+R indicators; Croissant descriptor present
FAIRness.L3: Croissant with responsible-AI annotations; persistent identifier; versioned release

Characterization.L3: Bias audit, coverage analysis, scope declared

Ethics.L3: Ethical oversight documented as metadata; access governance in place

Pre-model Explainability.L3: Feature lineage intact, linked to model cards

criteria.label: Persistent identifier assigned (DOI, ARK, or repository accession)
criteria.no_capture: Assigned by the repository at deposit. Nothing to record beforehand beyond which repository you intend to use.
criteria.remediation: Mint a DOI via Zenodo, DataCite, or your institutional repository before publishing. The identifier must resolve to a landing page that describes the dataset.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks the syntax: a DOI (10.NNNN/suffix) or an ARK. Whether it resolves is not checked offline, so confirm the landing page loads before you deposit.

criteria.label: Landing page URL with human-readable metadata
criteria.no_capture: Generated by the repository at deposit, so the URL does not exist until then.
criteria.remediation: Most repositories generate a landing page automatically when you mint a DOI. Confirm the page is publicly resolvable.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks that the value is an absolute, well-formed URL. That the page is public and describes the dataset is yours to confirm.

criteria.label: Metadata exposed in a machine-readable format (DataCite, schema.org/Dataset, or JSON-LD)
criteria.no_capture: Emitted by the repository from what you deposit. Check it once the deposit exists.
criteria.remediation: Confirm the landing page emits DataCite metadata or schema.org/Dataset JSON-LD. Most generalist repositories do this by default.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare this. The evidence is the landing page itself. View its source for DataCite or schema.org/Dataset JSON-LD, or run it through a structured-data testing tool.

criteria.label: Access protocol documented (open download, request form, or controlled-access process)
criteria.collection_hint: Decide early how a user will obtain the data — open download, registration, an agreement, a committee review — because the consent wording has to match the route you pick.
criteria.remediation: State explicitly how a user obtains the data: open download, registration, DUA, or DAC review.
criteria.verification_hint: The data steward confirms this by reading the access statement as a stranger would, and checking it names the actual route: a download link, a request form, or the committee that reviews requests.

criteria.label: Explicit, machine-readable license

beyond_cell.note: The cell names FAIR F+A indicators, and an explicit licence is R1.1. It is required at L1 because a release without one defaults to all-rights-reserved, which blocks the reuse every higher level assumes. The paper lists it as a release component and as an ethical condition of use.

criteria.collection_hint: Choose the licence before collection where you can: what you may release is bounded by the terms of every input and by what participants agreed to.
criteria.remediation: Pick a Creative Commons or Open Data Commons license. 'No license' defaults to all-rights-reserved and blocks reuse.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks the value against the bundled SPDX and Creative Commons identifiers, so a free-text licence name fails here.

criteria.label: Croissant 1.0 descriptor present and validates against the MLCommons schema
criteria.collection_hint: Keep the release's file list current as files are produced — names, formats, checksums. The descriptor is assembled from that list, and a list kept current as you go is the one that stays accurate.
criteria.remediation: Use the in-app Croissant generator. Including a descriptor at L1 makes the dataset directly ML-loadable today and trivially upgradable to L2.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool validates the descriptor against the Croissant 1.0 structure and reports any open recommendations. The Conformance step shows which rung of the machine-actionability ladder it reaches.

criteria.label: Variable terms drawn from recognised controlled vocabularies where applicable
criteria.collection_hint: As you name each field, note the published term it corresponds to. The correspondence is obvious while you are choosing the name and guesswork six months on.
criteria.remediation: Map clinical fields to LOINC/SNOMED, units to UCUM, climate vars to CF, etc. Document the mapping in the Croissant descriptor. Where the right vocabulary for your field is not obvious, look it up in FAIRsharing, the DCC Disciplinary Metadata Catalogue, or the RDA Metadata Standards Catalog before coining your own.
criteria.verification_hint: The domain expert confirms that each term comes from a published vocabulary and that its version is recorded. Which vocabulary applies is a disciplinary judgement, so look it up in FAIRsharing before coining a term.

criteria.label: Links to related datasets, schemas, or ontologies (qualified references)
criteria.collection_hint: Record the identifier of every dataset, schema, or ontology you draw on as you use it, with the relation: version of, part of, derived from.
criteria.remediation: Include `isVersionOf`, `isPartOf`, `references`, or schema.org/sameAs links so machines can navigate between related artefacts.
criteria.verification_hint: The data steward confirms this by following every link and checking it resolves to the artifact the relation claims it does.

criteria.label: Croissant descriptor includes Responsible-AI annotations (intended use, known limitations, sensitive attributes)
criteria.collection_hint: While you are deciding what the data is for, write the one-line intended use and the uses you would object to. Both are easier to state before there are results to defend.
criteria.remediation: Populate the Croissant `rai:` namespace fields. The in-app generator surfaces them when Pathway C is selected.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks that at least one rai: field in the descriptor carries content. Whether the intended use is stated well enough is covered by the scope and bias-audit rows.

criteria.label: Versioned release with concept-level and version-level identifiers; immutable per version
criteria.collection_hint: Fix the version string for this cut of the data, and note what would make you cut the next one.
criteria.remediation: Use a repository that mints both a concept DOI (resolves to latest) and version-specific DOIs (Zenodo and DataCite both support this).
criteria.verification_hint: The data steward confirms that the repository minted both a concept DOI and a version DOI, and that the files behind this version are frozen.

criteria.label: Deposition repository selected with appropriate access tier
criteria.collection_hint: Pick the target repository early and read its submission requirements: some constrain formats, consent wording, or file layout in ways that are cheap to satisfy before collection and expensive after.

beyond_cell.note: The cell names the Croissant annotations, the identifier, and the versioned release. Repository choice appears in the paper as a release component, outside the matrix cells. It is required here because the target repository constrains formats, consent wording, and access tier.

criteria.remediation: The options are scoped to your pathway and, in Pathway C, to your sub-domain — a domain repository is preferred over a generalist one, and any target recommended for your sub-domain is listed first. Record the repository you will deposit in and the access tier it will carry (open, registered, restricted, controlled, or embargoed). If the right repository is not listed, use Custom.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare this. The evidence is the repository's own submission policy, which states the access tiers it supports and the formats it accepts.

criteria.label: Original sources of the data described in prose (instruments, registries, surveys, or upstream datasets)
criteria.collection_hint: Name every source as you draw on it — instrument, registry, survey, or upstream dataset — with its version or the date you retrieved it. A source consulted and never written down is invisible by the time anyone asks.
criteria.remediation: Add a 'Sources' section to the README or datasheet listing every upstream source and how it was obtained.
criteria.verification_hint: The data engineer confirms that every upstream source named is one the project can account for, and that none used in practice is missing.

criteria.label: When and where the data was collected (time window, geography or instrument)
criteria.collection_hint: Note the first and last dates of collection as they happen, and the sites or instruments in scope. A window reconstructed from file timestamps months later is wrong in ways nobody can check.
criteria.remediation: State the inclusive collection dates and any geographic/cohort constraints. This is what downstream users need to judge fit.
criteria.verification_hint: The domain expert confirms the stated window and geography against what was collected. Only someone who was there catches a wrong date.

criteria.label: Every curation and transformation step listed in prose (cleaning, harmonisation, derivation rules)
criteria.collection_hint: Write each cleaning, harmonisation, or derivation step down as you apply it, with why you applied it. The step that seemed obvious at the time is the one nobody can reconstruct later.
criteria.remediation: List each step with inputs, outputs, and rationale. The PROV-O generator produces a structured version of this — write the prose first, encode it second.
criteria.verification_hint: The data engineer confirms this by walking the pipeline and checking that every step which touched the data appears in the list.

criteria.label: Software, scripts, and library versions used to produce the released dataset
criteria.collection_hint: Freeze the environment when the pipeline runs — a lock file, an image digest, a commit hash. Versions drift underneath you, and the number you remember is rarely the one that ran.
criteria.remediation: Capture interpreter version, library pins (requirements.txt or environment.yml), and a Git commit hash for in-house code.
criteria.verification_hint: The data engineer confirms these against the environment that produced the release — a lock file, an image digest, a commit hash.

criteria.label: PROV-O JSON-LD record accompanies the released dataset
criteria.collection_hint: Keep the run log the record is built from: for every processing step, its inputs, its outputs, and when it ran.
criteria.remediation: Use the in-app PROV-O generator for short pipelines, or export from CWL / Snakemake / Nextflow / Galaxy for long ones. The record is an RDF graph, so SHACL shape constraints check it beyond parsing.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks that the record parses as JSON-LD with a prov namespace, a graph, and at least one Entity. Run Deep validate on the Provenance tab to check the SHACL shapes.

criteria.label: PROV record contains an Entity per dataset version and per declared variable
criteria.collection_hint: List every variable you will release. For derived ones, note which variables they were computed from.
criteria.remediation: Variable-level Entities enable feature-lineage queries downstream. The in-app generator emits one Entity per variable when the variable list is populated.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool counts Entities carrying kind: variable. It cannot know which variables you left out, so completeness is yours to confirm.

criteria.label: PROV record contains an Activity per curation/transformation step, with parameters and software version
criteria.collection_hint: At run time, record the parameters used and the exact software version. Version numbers are the first thing to become unrecoverable.
criteria.remediation: Each Activity records `prov:used` (inputs), `prov:wasGeneratedBy` (outputs), parameters, and the software Agent that ran it.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks that at least one Activity records its software or its inputs. That every processing step has one is yours to confirm.

criteria.label: Agents declared with CRediT-style stakeholder roles
criteria.collection_hint: Note who ran each step, by ORCID, and in what role.
criteria.remediation: Name a data steward, domain expert, data engineer, ML practitioner, and governance officer — even if the same person holds multiple roles in a small team.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks that at least one Agent carries a role drawn from the stakeholder-role vocabulary.

criteria.label: Schema declared: types, units, and allowed values per variable
criteria.collection_hint: Fill in the type, the unit, and the allowed values as each column is defined. A value set retrofitted from the data recovers only what happened to appear in it. The permitted range has to be written down as you define the column.
criteria.remediation: Ship a data dictionary (CSV, Markdown, or DDI XML) listing every variable with its type, units, and value set.
criteria.verification_hint: The domain expert confirms every variable has a type, a unit where one applies, and a value set. Frictionless can check a declared table schema against the released data.

criteria.label: Total record count and basic shape (rows × columns, or equivalent)

beyond_cell.note: The cell names the declared schema. Record count is the other half of the composition summary a data card carries, and is the cheapest characterisation evidence there is.

criteria.no_capture: Counted from the released files, so it is computed at write-up, once the files are final.
criteria.remediation: One sentence in the README. Trivial to provide and always missed.
criteria.verification_hint: The data engineer confirms the stated count against the released files. It is a one-line check, and the one most often skipped.

criteria.label: Missingness rates per variable
criteria.collection_hint: The rates can be computed later. The reasons cannot. Note why values are missing as it happens — an instrument fault, a refusal, a question added mid-study.
criteria.remediation: Report % missing per variable. Default missingness handling encodes fairness properties — disclose what was applied.
criteria.verification_hint: The data engineer confirms the rates were computed from the released files themselves. Great Expectations or Pandera produce them as a profiling report.

criteria.label: Summary statistics per variable (numeric: min/max/mean/std; categorical: value counts)
criteria.no_capture: Computed from the released files. What is worth noting as you go is anything that would make a summary misleading — see the missingness and known-errors rows.
criteria.remediation: A one-page summary or a Great-Expectations / Pandera profiling report. Include in the documentation bundle.
criteria.verification_hint: The data engineer confirms the summaries match the released data. A profiling report from Great Expectations, Pandera, or Deequ is the usual source.

criteria.label: Known errors and their treatment (corrected, flagged, dropped, or left in)
criteria.collection_hint: Log each error as you find it and what you did about it: corrected, flagged, dropped, or left in. The decision is the part that disappears. The error usually leaves a trace.
criteria.remediation: Explicit disclosure beats silent correction. List known issues even if you chose not to fix them.
criteria.verification_hint: The domain expert confirms the list reflects what is known, including issues nobody fixed. Only someone close to the data can say what is missing from it.

criteria.label: Class balance for classification targets (where applicable; mark N/A otherwise)
criteria.no_capture: Counted from the released labels. Nothing to record in advance beyond whether the dataset has a classification target at all.
criteria.remediation: Report counts per class. Heavy imbalance affects evaluation metrics — surfacing it lets reviewers judge fit.
criteria.verification_hint: The ML practitioner confirms the counts per class, or that the dataset carries no classification target and the row is marked N/A.

criteria.label: Bias audit: representation parity across protected attributes and curation-induced skew
criteria.collection_hint: Record the attributes you will need to audit representation on — site, instrument, batch, demographic group — as structured columns in the data. You cannot audit what was never captured.
criteria.remediation: Use Aequitas, Fairlearn, or an equivalent tool. Compare distributions before and after curation, so introduced skew surfaces alongside released-state parity.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare this. The evidence is the audit report itself. Aequitas or Fairlearn produce one — link it in the note field, and cover both the pre-curation and released distributions.

criteria.label: Temporal, geographic, demographic, and modality coverage analysis
criteria.collection_hint: Note the span the data actually covers: dates, sites, instruments, populations, modalities. Also note what you intended to cover and did not.
criteria.remediation: List subgroups represented and subgroups missing. Coverage gaps constrain valid downstream uses.
criteria.verification_hint: The domain expert confirms the stated coverage against the sampling design, and names the subgroups that are absent as well as those present.

criteria.label: Intended uses and out-of-scope uses declared explicitly
criteria.collection_hint: Write down the question this data was collected to answer. That sentence becomes the intended-use statement.
criteria.remediation: State both: tasks the dataset should support, and tasks it should not (e.g., 'not for clinical decision support').
criteria.verification_hint: The domain expert and the ML practitioner agree on both halves: the tasks this data supports, and the tasks it should not be used for.

criteria.label: Known selection effects, measurement error, and confounders documented
criteria.collection_hint: Keep a running note of anything that went wrong or changed mid-stream: a failed batch, a recalibration, an amended protocol, a site that dropped out.

beyond_cell.note: The cell names the bias audit, the coverage analysis, and the scope declaration. Known selection effects, measurement error, and confounders are the fourth row of the characterization record the paper prescribes.

criteria.remediation: Healthcare-utilisation proxies, exclusion windows, instrument quirks — name them. Downstream users need them to judge transferability.
criteria.verification_hint: The domain expert confirms this. A limitation that nobody involved in collection names is unlikely to be discoverable afterwards.

criteria.label: Consent basis recorded (or explicit non-applicability)
criteria.collection_hint: File the consent form or the waiver alongside the data when collection is approved, and note which document establishes the basis. This is the row that most often cannot be repaired afterwards.
criteria.remediation: Document what consent covers — including 'not applicable' for non-human-subjects or already-public data.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare this. The evidence is the consent form or the IRB waiver that establishes the basis. Nothing mechanical can confirm the basis covers the use you intend.

criteria.label: Direct identifiers removed or transformed
criteria.collection_hint: Record which fields were removed or transformed at the moment you do it, and keep the script. "We de-identified it" does not expand back into a list of fields.
criteria.remediation: Names, contact details, MRNs, exact addresses, exact dates of service. Indirect identifiers come at L2.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare this. The evidence is the de-identification run — the script, the tool's report, or a reviewer's sign-off on the released files.

criteria.label: De-identification method recorded (which standard, which parameters)
criteria.collection_hint: Note the method and its parameters as they are chosen — the k, the epsilon, the Safe Harbor checklist — together with who decided.
criteria.remediation: Record the method and its parameters: HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity (with k), differential privacy (with ε). A phrase like 'stripped names' leaves a reviewer to guess which of these you did.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare the method. The evidence is the report that names it with its parameters — k for k-anonymity, epsilon for differential privacy, or the Safe Harbor checklist.

criteria.label: Ethics oversight documented as metadata (approving body, protocol ID, approval date, scope of permitted use, expiry/renewal status)
criteria.collection_hint: Record the approving body, protocol number, and approval date at the moment approval is granted. By writing-up time the letter is usually filed away.
criteria.remediation: The review itself happens before/during acquisition. What travels with the dataset at L3 is structured evidence of that review — that is the L3 requirement.
criteria.verification_hint: The governance officer confirms the recorded approval matches the letter on file: body, protocol number, date, scope of permitted use, and current status.

criteria.label: Tiered access governance in place (open / registered / restricted / controlled / embargoed)
criteria.collection_hint: Decide before collection who will be allowed access and under what conditions — consent wording usually has to match the access tier you intend.
criteria.remediation: Match the access tier to the sensitivity of the data and the consent basis recorded at L1.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare the tier. The evidence is the repository's access configuration, which a reviewer can see from the landing page without asking you.

criteria.label: Data-use agreement template referenced if access is restricted or controlled (mark N/A for open access)
criteria.collection_hint: If access will be restricted, note which data-use agreement applies, or that one still has to be drafted.
criteria.remediation: Link to the DUA template the requester signs. Repositories like PhysioNet ship one. Institutional Dataverse instances often do too.
criteria.verification_hint: The governance officer confirms the referenced agreement is the one a requester actually signs, or that open access makes it inapplicable.

criteria.label: Current data access contact named (person, role, or committee, with a durable address)
criteria.collection_hint: Decide who fields access requests, and give the role a durable address. Individuals move institutions. The dataset outlives them.
criteria.remediation: The ethics evidence at L3 is only actionable if a requester can reach someone. Name the data access committee, the steward's role, or the study contact, and give an address that survives staff turnover: a role alias, or the contact route your repository provides.
criteria.verification_hint: The governance officer confirms the address reaches someone today. This is the one row that decays without anybody editing it.

criteria.label: Whether secondary use is permitted, and under what constraints
criteria.collection_hint: Record what the consent or licence actually permits beyond this study, in the words the document uses.
criteria.remediation: Bound by what consent basis at L1 supports. Be explicit — silence here defaults reviewers to 'not permitted'.
criteria.verification_hint: The governance officer confirms the stated permission is bounded by the consent basis recorded at L1. Claiming more here than the consent supports is the failure mode.

criteria.label: Every variable has a human-readable definition
criteria.collection_hint: Write the sentence defining each variable when you create it, while what it measures is still precise in your head.
criteria.remediation: Give each variable a sentence explaining what it measures and how it was measured. A column name abbreviates. A definition tells a stranger what was captured.
criteria.verification_hint: The domain expert confirms each definition would let a stranger interpret the column without asking a question.

criteria.label: Units recorded for every measured variable
criteria.collection_hint: Take the unit from the instrument or the protocol at the moment of measurement, in UCUM where a code exists. A bare number is not convertible afterwards.
criteria.remediation: Use UCUM where applicable. Untyped numerics are a frequent cause of merge errors across cohorts.
criteria.verification_hint: The domain expert confirms the units against the instrument or the protocol, in UCUM where a code exists.

criteria.label: Derived variables traceable to source variable(s) and the operation that produced them
criteria.collection_hint: As each derived variable is created, note its source variables and the operation that produced it. The feature-lineage row at L3 needs the same note, so write it once.
criteria.remediation: BMI = mass / height² is a source-and-operation. Record the source variables and the operation alongside the derived value.
criteria.verification_hint: The data engineer confirms each derived variable names its sources and its operation closely enough to recompute it.

criteria.label: Encodings documented (one-hot, normalisation, tokenisation, vocabulary mappings)
criteria.collection_hint: Save the encoder, tokenizer, or normalisation configuration with the run that fitted it. The mapping cannot be inferred back from encoded values.
criteria.remediation: If the released artefact is post-encoding, ship the encoder configuration / tokenizer alongside it.
criteria.verification_hint: The ML practitioner confirms the shipped encoder or tokenizer configuration reproduces the encoded values in the release.

criteria.label: Feature lineage preserved end-to-end via the PROV record
criteria.collection_hint: As you create each derived variable, note its source variables and the operation that produced it.
criteria.remediation: Every released feature can be reconstructed from raw inputs by following the PROV record's `wasDerivedFrom` chain.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks that every variable Entity in the PROV record has a wasDerivedFrom edge, so no released feature is an orphan.

criteria.label: Released alongside or linkable to a model card (when models trained on this data exist)
criteria.collection_hint: If a model will be trained on this data, note where its model card will live.
criteria.remediation: Triangular linkage: dataset DOI ↔ model DOI/HF ID ↔ results DOI. Link bidirectionally so each artefact resolves to the others. Where what ships is a deployed system, a system card is the equivalent artifact — it documents the safety mitigations and tool access around the model as well as the model itself.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare this. The evidence is the model card resolving at the URL you give, with a link back to this dataset so the pair can be traced from either end.

criteria.label: Released in an open, non-proprietary format
criteria.collection_hint: Choose the export format at the instrument or in the job script, before a proprietary container becomes the only copy you have.
criteria.remediation: Parquet / CSV for tabular; HDF5 / NetCDF / Zarr for arrays; DICOM / NIfTI for imaging. Avoid Excel, SAS, or vendor formats as the canonical release.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks the declared format against the bundled open-format lists for tabular, array, and imaging data.

criteria.label: Total size and per-file size reported
criteria.no_capture: Measured from the deposited files at release.
criteria.remediation: One line in the README. Lets downstream users plan downloads and storage.
criteria.verification_hint: The data engineer confirms the stated sizes against the deposited files.

criteria.label: Long-term access plan (institutional commitment, repository SLA, or migration strategy)

beyond_cell.note: The cell names the storage footprint. Long-term access is the stewardship layer the paper argues is the rate-limiting factor for AI adoption in science, and it is a property of the deposit, which no inspection of the file can reveal.

criteria.collection_hint: Settle where the data will live for the long term while you can still choose. Note the repository and the commitment behind it.
criteria.remediation: Use a repository with an institutional commitment (Zenodo's CERN backing, institutional Dataverse, etc.), which outlives a personal server or a lab machine.
criteria.verification_hint: The data steward confirms the commitment exists outside this project — a repository policy or an institutional undertaking that outlives the team.

criteria.label: Maintenance stated: update cadence, how superseded versions are deprecated, and a channel for errata

beyond_cell.source: Paper §2.7 (Maintenance, versioning and long-term stewardship); Figure 7 (fig:data-card-example), Maintenance row
beyond_cell.note: The cell names the storage footprint. Post-release obligations are the other half of a release target: a dataset offered as a community asset with no stated cadence, no deprecation of superseded versions, and no way to report an error makes every project start the lifecycle over. Set at L2 because that is the threshold the paper ties to publication as a community asset.

criteria.collection_hint: Write down now what would make you cut a new version, and who would announce it. Both are cheap to decide before release and awkward to invent after a user reports an error.
criteria.remediation: Three sentences: how often the dataset is expected to change, what happens to a superseded version (kept and marked deprecated, or withdrawn), and where a user reports a suspected error. Keep superseded versions resolvable and marked deprecated: a model trained on v1 stays reproducible only while v1 resolves.
criteria.verification_hint: The data steward confirms all three are stated: the cadence, what happens to a superseded version, and where a user reports an error.

criteria.label: At least one data-centric efficiency intervention applied (curation / distillation / active learning / curriculum)
criteria.collection_hint: If you curate, distil, or subsample before release, record what you removed and why. That decision is invisible in the released file.
criteria.remediation: Document which intervention was applied and the metric it improved (records removed, accuracy at matched compute, etc.).
criteria.verification_hint: You declare the intervention. The evidence is the measurement that motivated it — records removed, compression ratio, or accuracy at a matched compute budget.

criteria.label: Compute cost of producing this release reported (compute hours, hardware type, energy or estimated emissions)
criteria.collection_hint: Note the compute this release consumed as you go: core-hours or instance-hours, the machine, and how many runs. Schedulers report it, and queue history rolls over.
criteria.remediation: Bind these figures to the same release bundle as the datasheet and PROV record. Without disclosure, efficiency claims are unverifiable.
criteria.verification_hint: The data engineer confirms the figures against the scheduler's accounting, while the queue history still holds them.

criteria.label: Loadable in a standard scientific-computing environment (pandas, numpy, R, or domain-equivalent)
criteria.no_capture: Follows from the release format, so the open-format decision settles it.
criteria.remediation: If a reviewer can't `pd.read_parquet(path)` or its domain equivalent, the format is wrong.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool infers this from the declared format: a recognised open format is loadable in a standard environment. It does not open your files.

criteria.label: Codebook or data dictionary shipped alongside the data

beyond_cell.note: The cell names loadability in a standard environment. A codebook is what makes the loaded table interpretable, and the paper lists it in the release bundle alongside the README and the validation report.

criteria.collection_hint: Keep the per-column notes in one place as you make them. The codebook is assembled from them, and gathering them at the end is the expensive way to do it.
criteria.remediation: Variable name, type, units, value set, and a one-sentence description per field. Markdown, CSV, or DDI all work.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare this. The evidence is the codebook in the release bundle. Frictionless can check a declared table schema against the data it describes.

criteria.label: Field values map to recognised controlled vocabularies where applicable (LOINC / SNOMED / UCUM / CF / ICD-10 / etc.)
criteria.collection_hint: For coded values, note the code system and its version at the time of coding. ICD-10 and ICD-11 codes look alike and do not mean the same thing.
criteria.remediation: Without controlled vocabularies, two correctly-documented datasets still cannot be aligned. Record the vocabulary version alongside its name.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare this. The evidence is the mapping itself — each field to its vocabulary term, with the vocabulary version. A domain validator checks it where one exists for your field.

criteria.label: Schemas referenced as linked external schemas (DDI, BIDS, CF-conventions, schema.org)
criteria.collection_hint: Note the URL of any schema or standard you are conforming to while you are conforming to it.
criteria.remediation: Reference the schema by URL inside the Croissant descriptor's `conformsTo` field.
criteria.verification_hint: You declare this. The evidence is the conformsTo reference in the descriptor resolving to the schema you name.

criteria.label: Croissant descriptor enables direct load into ML frameworks without custom parsing
criteria.collection_hint: As files are produced, list them and the columns inside them, with types and units.
criteria.remediation: Verify with `mlcroissant` reference library: a four-line load (see Code Block 2 in the source paper) should yield records.
criteria.verification_hint: The tool checks that the descriptor declares at least one file and one record set with fields, which is what a loader needs. Round-trip it through mlcroissant to certify the executable rung.

criteria.label: Example load snippet provided (TensorFlow Datasets, Hugging Face, or PyTorch DataLoader)
criteria.collection_hint: Keep the few lines you yourself used to load the data. That is the snippet.
criteria.remediation: Five lines of Python in the README that load the dataset and print one record. Removes ambiguity that prose cannot.
criteria.verification_hint: The ML practitioner confirms the snippet by running it against the released files from a clean environment.
